chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who carried foodstuff with another man in a ship, and it was deficient, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is liable.' I said, 'Perhaps it increased.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you know that it increased by anything?' I said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is for you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on excess or deficiency of shared cargo in a ship according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of *daman* (liability) in shared maritime transport, distinguishing between loss and gain based on the carrier's knowledge. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the carrier's subjective awareness (*'ilm*) when determining ownership of surplus cargo, ensuring fairness in commercial contracts. This ruling underscores the importance of transparency and trust (*amanah*) in Islamic trade practices.
